newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sees $300-400 mln in petrochem investment.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sees $300-400 mln in petrochem investment.

text.p: Mexico expects a first wave of private investment next year in its petrochemical industry to raise $300-400 million, which would be used to support investment in existing plants, Energy Minister Jesus Reyes Heroles told reporters Thursday.

Reyes Heroles said after opening a chemical industry conference here that "the first package of investment next year, speaking ideally, is that we would attract about $300 million to $400 million to support investments we have planned for plants in the industry".

Mexico earlier this month announced a new plan for attracting private investment into its petrochemical industry, offering foreigners up to 49 percent of existing plants and allowing them to take 100 percent of new projects.

Reyes Heroles did not give an exact date for the first sales of stakes in existing plants, which will be grouped into around 13 or 14 separate subsidiaries of state oil giant Pemex's petrochemicals division and run along commercial lines in preparation for the sale.

But he said: "The plan is....to initiate the placement of 49 percent of stock of the new public petrochemical companies by the middle of next year for the purpose of financing urgent investment to eliminate bottlenecks".
